question: Should OpenClaw accept confirmation-gated local archive and the new trusted plugin session/delegated-execution contracts for this phase-one Codex supervision release?
rationale: Codex provides process-local status and a bare persistent archive mutation but no cross-process lease, while the PR also establishes durable public plugin ownership APIs that code review cannot accept on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Accept bounded design
options.body: Approve the narrow APIs, snapshot-branch continuation, and confirmation-gated local archive while keeping paired-node sessions read-only and documenting the independent-runner limitation.

options.title: Defer archive
options.body: Approve continuation and the session APIs but remove archive until Codex exposes cross-process ownership fencing.

options.title: Narrow API surface
options.body: Keep the new session and delegation machinery private to Codex until maintainers decide which seams should become external plugin contracts.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded design
recommendation.body: Approve the narrow APIs, snapshot-branch continuation, and confirmation-gated local archive while keeping paired-node sessions read-only and documenting the independent-runner limitation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced and currently owns most of the merged Codex harness, app-server, plugin runtime, and macOS integration surfaces involved in this decision.
